title: The effect of item reordering on psychometric properties and student achievement: The evidence from health technicians’ education
abstract: Background and Objective: The use of multiple test forms with different item and option orders is a common strategy to reduce cheating in large-enrollment educational settings. However, concerns remain regarding whether such structural modifications may affect psychometric properties and student achievement. This study examined whether altering the order of test items and response options influences test reliability, item characteristics, and student performance in health technician education programs. Methods: We used an experimental pretest–posttest control group design with 122 students enrolled in health technician education programs. We administered a 20-item multiple-choice biology achievement test in parallel forms that differed only in item order and response options. Psychometric properties were evaluated using KR-20 reliability coefficients, item difficulty indices, and item discrimination indices. We analyzed differences among test forms using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and two-sample Z-tests. In addition, students’ self-reported interest in biology and perceived prior knowledge were examined in relation to achievement outcomes. Results: No statistically significant differences were found among the test forms in reliability coefficients, item difficulty indices, item discrimination indices, or posttest achievement scores (p > .05). These findings indicate psychometric equivalence across the forms. In contrast, students reporting higher levels of interest in biology and stronger perceived prior knowledge achieved significantly higher scores than their peers (p < .01), with moderate-to-large effect sizes. Descriptive findings further showed that a considerable proportion of students reported low interest in biology (37.7%) and insufficient subject knowledge (77.7%). Conclusions: The findings suggest that structural modifications such as reordering test items and response options do not compromise measurement quality or student achievement. Instead, learner-related variables appear to play a more substantial role in academic performance. The study adds empirical evidence to the limited literature on test form equivalence in vocational health education contexts and supports using parallel test forms as a practical approach to enhancing examination security while maintaining psychometric consistency.

title: ورک پلیس ایتھکس: سیرت طیبہ ﷺ کی روشنی میں اطلاقی مطالعہ
abstract: In the contemporary era, ethical values have become increasingly significant in professional and organizational life. The success, development, and sustainability of any organization depend not only on professional competence and economic resources but also on ethical conduct, mutual trust, honesty, integrity, justice, benevolence, responsibility, and accountability among employees and management. Workplace ethics refers to the moral principles and values that guide individuals' behavior, professional responsibilities, interpersonal relationships, and organizational affairs within the workplace. In the modern workplace, issues such as corruption, injustice, favoritism, lack of transparency, breach of promises, and violation of employees' rights have created a growing need for a comprehensive ethical framework capable of guiding both individuals and organizations. The present study, entitled "Workplace Ethics: An Applied Study in the Light of Seerah Tayyibah (The Prophetic Biography)", examines professional and organizational ethics in the light of the life and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). The primary objective of this research is to explore how the ethical principles demonstrated in the Seerah of the Prophet (ﷺ) can be practically applied to contemporary workplaces and organizational environments. The study focuses on fundamental ethical principles derived from the Qur'an, Sunnah, and Seerah, including justice and fairness, trustworthiness and integrity, truthfulness, benevolence, responsibility, transparency, fulfillment of promises, consultation, respect for human dignity, employees' rights, and leadership and managerial responsibilities. The research analyzes relevant books, scholarly literature, research articles, and other academic sources while examining the practical dimensions of workplace ethics. The findings indicate that the ethical principles embodied in the Seerah of the Prophet (ﷺ) provide a comprehensive and balanced framework capable of strengthening individual character as well as improving organizational management, leadership, employee rights, and workplace relationships. The practical implementation of Prophetic ethical teachings in modern organizations can promote trust, transparency, justice, accountability, and professional integrity while reducing corruption, exploitation, injustice, and unethical practices. In light of the findings, the study recommends incorporating the ethical principles of the Seerah Tayyibah into organizational training programs, professional development, and character-building initiatives. Such an approach can contribute to the development of a positive, just, trustworthy, and ethically responsible workplace culture. It can not only enhance organizational performance and professional conduct but also contribute to the promotion of moral and human values in society. This research titled "Workplace Ethics in the Light of Seerat -un-Nabi ﷺ: An Applied Study" aims to evaluate the current workplace ethics in HBL Bank, Times University, and FG Degree College Multan and to compare them with the principles of Seerat-un-Nabi ﷺ. For this purpose, data was collected from 130 employees through a 30 item questionnaire using a 5point Likert scale. The findings revealed that the overall score of workplace ethics in all three institutions was 2.75 out of 5, which is unsatisfactory. The major issues identified were lack of honesty, injustice, ethical decline, and absence of servant leadership. The study concludes that the principles of honesty, justice, compassion, consultation, and service found in the Seerah of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ provide the most effective solution to modern workplace problems. Based on these findings, practical recommendations have been proposed for all three institutions. Implementing these ethical principles can significantly improve organizational performance and employee satisfaction.
reasoning_research: The abstract reports a survey of 130 employees using a 30-item Likert questionnaire across three institutions, but provides limited methodological detail on sampling, validity, reliability, statistical analysis, or preregistration. The study is also heavily normative and based on religious textual analysis, which reduces empirical rigor and reproducibility.
reasoning_impact: Workplace ethics, honesty, justice, and trust are relevant to moral decision-making and social norms, but the study is descriptive, context-specific, and does not engage with decision-neuroscience or computational theory. Its likely influence is mainly within applied religious ethics and organizational management rather than self-control or attention research.

title: Incentivizing Honesty in Two-Sided Information Markets: An Evolutionary Game Approach to Crowdsourcing Trust
abstract: Ensuring trustworthy participation in decentralized crowdsourcing platforms is a key challenge in information systems research, where strategic heterogeneity, bounded rationality, and lack of centralized enforcement limit classical equilibrium approaches. This study proposes a bi-population game-theoretic framework with state-dependent payoffs, where reputation modeled via a sigmoid function of contribution frequency and accuracy directly shapes incentives for interdependent providers and users. This gives rise to a bi-population replicator framework with state-dependent payoffs, where the evolutionary dynamics of each population are driven by reputation-adjusted incentive differentials. We analyze the boundary equilibria of the resulting system and characterize stability through reputation-dependent incentive thresholds. We show analytically that the honest boundary equilibrium (x, y) = (1, 1) is locally asymptotically stable if and only if (β+δ)R>C−ϕ. We also derive the evolutionarily stable strategy (ESS) condition for the honest strategy in the research of Maynard Smith and Price, where the ESS condition depends on the state-dependent payoff structure. We show that the ESS condition for the honest strategy is progressively relaxed as the agents accumulate more reputation through honest behavior over time. This gives rise to a novel dynamic stability feedback phenomenon wherein the stability condition for the honest equilibrium becomes progressively relaxed as the agents accumulate more reputation through honest behavior over time. The transient dynamics may exhibit nonlinear adjustment patterns due to the gradual evolution of reputation variables, characterized by nonlinear transient adjustment patterns consistent with findings in eco-evolutionary and environmental-feedback modeling. Simulation results, which are based on fifty independent simulation runs with varying initial conditions (x(0) = y(0) ∈ {0.3, 0.5, 0.8}), support the convergence behavior toward the honest equilibrium for the default parameter setup. The sensitivity analysis suggests a non-monotonic performance profile for varying honesty levels γ, which implies an optimal range for γ ∈ [0.55, 0.70]. The main factor for equilibrium honesty is identified as the direct dishonesty penalty φ. As a conclusion, this model provides valuable insights for the design of incentive-compatible crowdsourcing mechanisms, which are supported by analytical results. Future work will focus on empirical validation.

title: Belief updating under strategic deception: Evidence from a classroom voting game
abstract: This paper introduces a classroom game, adapted from the television series The Traitors , that integrates six core concepts from game theory and behavioural economics into a single 25-min activity: asymmetric information, cheap talk, pooling equilibrium, Bayesian updating, information cascades, and behavioural biases. Six volunteer students are secretly assigned hidden roles as Faithfuls or Traitors, and the class must identify and banish the Traitors through iterative rounds of discussion and plurality voting. Observations from a pilot implementation are suggestive of the targeted mechanisms: pooling behaviour among Traitors, cascade-driven voting in early rounds, base rate neglect, and confirmation bias elicited by deliberately random observations planted on role cards. The paper provides a structured debrief protocol aligned to the experiential learning cycle, a round-by-round belief elicitation instrument based on proper scoring rules, a five-item pre/post concept assessment with a delayed retention option, analysis code, and a complete facilitator pack, enabling instructors to replicate the activity and to generate quantitative evidence on learning.

title: TANTANGAN DAN PENGEMBANGAN DISPOSISI MIPA (SIKAP, KEBIASAAN BERPIKIR, DAN PERILAKU BELAJAR) DALAM PEMBELAJARAN DI ERA DIGITAL DAN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed the teaching and learning of Mathematics and Natural Sciences (STEM). While offering opportunities for adaptive and personalized instruction, these intelligent tools also introduce critical challenges to students' affective dispositions, habits of mind, and autonomous learning behaviors. This study aims to map contemporary challenges and formulate pedagogical strategies for fostering STEM dispositions in the AI era. This research employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) guided by the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across international and national databases (Scopus, ERIC, SINTA, and Google Scholar) for publications between 2019 and 2026. Following systematic identification (n=100), screening (n=75), and eligibility assessment (n=30), 14 primary empirical articles were included. The synthesized findings demonstrate a dual paradox of AI integration. Unregulated use of generative AI platforms triggers cognitive offloading, superficial learning, academic dishonesty, and error blindness. Conversely, when integrated into active inquiry models (Guided Inquiry, STEM-IBSE) supported by Tiered AI Scaffolding, AI significantly reduces math anxiety, enhances self-efficacy, and fosters productive struggle. The study concludes that the successful development of STEM dispositions in the AI era relies on instructional design quality, metacognitive monitoring, and students' motivational persistence. ABSTRAK Perkembangan teknologi digital dan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah membawa transformasi mendasar dalam praktik pembelajaran Matematika dan Ilmu Pengetahuan Alam (MIPA). Di samping menghadirkan peluang pembelajaran adaptif dan personal, kehadiran teknologi pintar ini memicu tantangan serius terhadap aspek afektif, kebiasaan berpikir (habits of mind), dan kemandirian perilaku belajar siswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memetakan tantangan kontemporer serta merumuskan strategi pedagogis pengembangan disposisi MIPA pada era AI. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) yang berpedoman pada protokol PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses). Penelusuran literatur dilakukan pada basis data bereputasi (Scopus, ERIC, SINTA, dan Google Scholar) untuk publikasi periode 2019–2026. Melalui tahapan identifikasi (n=100), penyaringan (n=75), dan uji kelayakan (n=30), terpilih sebanyak 14 artikel primer yang memenuhi kriteria inklusi secara ketat. Hasil sintesis literatur menunjukkan bahwa pemanfaatan AI menghadirkan dampak paradoksal. Penggunaan platform AI generatif yang tidak terarah berisiko memicu ketergantungan kognitif (cognitive offloading), pembelajaran dangkal (superficial learning), degradasi kejujuran akademik, serta kebutaan terhadap kekeliruan luaran AI (error blindness). Sebaliknya, integrasi AI dalam model pembelajaran aktif berbasis inkuiri (Guided Inquiry, STEM-IBSE) yang didukung oleh perancah berjenjang (Tiered AI Scaffolding) terbukti efektif menurunkan kecemasan matematika (math anxiety), memperkuat efikasi diri, dan menumbuhkan daya juang produktif (productive struggle). Keberhasilan pengembangan disposisi MIPA di era AI ditentukan oleh sinergi antara desain instruksional guru, regulasi metakognitif, dan ketekunan motivasional (motivational persistence) peserta didik.
journal: SCIENCE Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Matematika dan IPA

title: The hidden Self - Self-identification in criminal situations
abstract: This study examined how crime-related contextual information modulates self-identification through auditory and visual identity cues. Using a simulated-crime paradigm, two experiments tested recognition of self-voice and self-face under three contextual conditions: self-relevant crime information, self-irrelevant crime information, and self-relevant non-crime information. Experiment 1 examined self-voice recognition. Participants responded faster under self-relevant contexts than under self-irrelevant crime information, suggesting that contextual self-relevance may facilitate auditory identity processing by increasing semantic engagement. Experiment 2 examined self-face recognition. Participants showed a self-face advantage under self-irrelevant crime and self-relevant non-crime contexts, but this advantage disappeared when crime-related information was directly linked to the self. Supplementary Ex-Gaussian analyses indicated that this modulation was mainly reflected in the μ parameter rather than in σ or τ, suggesting a shift in the central tendency of self-face responses rather than increased response variability or extreme slowing. Exploratory HDDM analyses further suggested that contextual effects were associated with changes in evidence accumulation.

title: Overinclusion but not social exclusion shifts sacrificial harm acceptance in online ostracism paradigm
abstract: Abstract The cognitive-motivational repercussions of social exclusion have been extensively studied, particularly its adverse effects on cognitive functions such as decision-making. However, its influence on moral decision-making remains underexplored. In an era where a significant portion of social interaction takes place online, social exclusion is increasingly manifested through a lack of digital attention. The present study therefore examined moral decision-making across different levels of inclusionary status using an online ostracism paradigm. This paradigm simulates social interaction on a mock social-media platform that mirrored the digital dynamics of social connection through Likes , whereby participants experienced exclusion ( N = 31; 1 Like), inclusion ( N = 30; 5 Likes) and overinclusion ( N = 30; 9 Likes). Across mixed-effects models and a dual frequentist–Bayesian approach, overinclusion was associated with greater acceptance of sacrificial harm in self-beneficiary moral dilemmas, whereas exclusion and inclusion did not differ. Over-included participants also reported lower arousal in response to the dilemmas, and mediation analyses provided evidence consistent with a partially arousal-mediated overinclusion effect (attenuated when controlling for empathy traits). Additionally, higher affective empathy traits were associated with a lower tendency for sacrificial harm. This study demonstrates that moral decision-making remains unaffected by the short-term social exclusion, whereas overinclusion promotes sacrificial harm acceptance through the partial mediation of arousal. We conclude by outlining testable accounts for the null effect of exclusion, while highlighting implications for chronically over-included online users (e.g., influencers), and reporting hypothesis-generating hierarchical drift-diffusion predictions for future work.
keywords: Psychology of Moral and Emotional Judgment
